sections.title: Player read-aloud
sections.body: The Clover Co-op climbs six stories up an ancient tree. The room smells of bread, moss tea, old wood, and somebody’s terrible but enthusiastic fiddle.

sections.title: Scene summary
sections.body: The party visits the Clover Co-op, the social heart of Hush.

sections.title: Player questions
items: What local custom in Hush reminds you of home?
Who accepts hospitality awkwardly, and who knows exactly what to do?
What small repaired object in the Co-op tells you this place survives by care?

sections.title: GM notes
items: Let players invent one cozy custom. Fold it into the epilogue.
Keep player-facing information actionable. Reveal systemic truth through objects, reactions, and consequences before naming it.
Manufactured-threat lens: seed the contradiction, do not explain it. The surface goal stays simple and heroic.
[ADD/GUARANTEED] A Grail "Protection Coverage" invoice hangs on the Clover Co-op wall, overdue and steep.

sections.title: Checks and rolls
items: Presence Accept hospitality without turning it into extraction. Easy Gain gifts and a Custodian warning. 10 Cleanly resolve: Accept hospitality without turning it into extraction. Add a concrete boon, extra clue, or improved position. Success, plus the player names one helpful detail or asks one follow-up question. Success, but the GM exposes a cost, ticks a countdown, or reveals a new pressure tied to The Clover Co-op. The full goal slips, but the party still learns a useful truth or avoids the worst consequence. The GM makes a hard move that follows from the fiction and leaves the next choice visible. Spend Fear to make trust cost time, reveal a local fear, or show a ward symptom that locals have normalized. On mixed or sliding results, reveal information in layers: visible fact, actionable clue, then systemic truth.

sections.title: Clues
items: Custodian warning Be kind to her. This unlocks a warmer Act Four. She is tired of being rushed and called a function.

sections.title: Loot
items: Use Clover Co-op gifts table
Sableleaf Shoes: A pair of shoes sewn entirely from broad sablewood leaves sits light as breath, green-veined, and already leaning toward motion.
Bugbane Berry™: A fat red-orange berry shines a little too perfectly, with a tiny insect suspended dead-center like a pit in amber. It looks appetizing and deeply wrong.
Sable Sap: Warm amber sap beads from a crack in a huge trunk like the tree is breathing it out. It smells of honey, woodsmoke, and something older.
Fire Wine™: A strong golden liquor sloshes in a thick jug, warm going down and warmer staying there. A paper tag insists it is not made from grapes and is absolutely not medicinal.

sections.title: Mechanics
items: Plot So Far: The party is in Act Three pressure: The party visits the Clover Co-op, the social heart of Hush.

Mechanics In Play: Use Daggerheart Duality Dice as baseline. Use the listed Difficulty and outcome options when a roll matters. Keep trivial actions no-roll; roll only when uncertainty, cost, or danger is interesting.

Roll Cards: s03-03-honor-the-co-op-custom S03-03 Honor the Co-op custom Honor the Co-op custom Presence Presence None 10 Presence makes courtesy active rather than performative. The party treats Hush like a checkpoint. Critical Success: best possible version of the action; gain Hope and clear 1 Stress. Add an extra benefit that follows from the fiction. Success with Hope: the PC gets what they wanted and gains Hope. Keep the position clean or generous. Success with Fear: the PC gets what they wanted, but the GM gains Fear and introduces a cost, complication, or pressure. Failure with Hope: the PC does not get the full result, but gains Hope and receives a useful thread, clue, or safer next option. Failure with Fear: the PC fails and the GM gains Fear. Make a hard move that follows from the fiction. The party treats Hush like a checkpoint. Use a hard complication, lost time, worse position, GM...
Gm Fear Spends: Make trust cost time, humility, or a public apology. Show a ward symptom locals have normalized because nobody official listened.
Conditions Hazards: No official condition unless a feature, hazard, or fictional position calls for Hidden, Restrained, or Vulnerable.
Search Loot Clues: Clover Co-op gifts: rolls, moss-honey, clover cord, safe path, field-care moss, Custodian warning.
No Roll Guidance: Do not call for a roll when the players have time, a clear method, and no meaningful pressure.
Escalation: Escalate by making cost visible: time, noise, trust, ward instability, or someone vulnerable in danger.
Deescalation: De-escalate through respect, care, honest testimony, useful evidence, or a concrete concession.
Tv Mechanics Caption: Public cue: The Clover Co-op asks what the party does, what it costs, and who is protected.

Trait Variety Note: Primary traits in this scene: Finesse, Knowledge, Presence. If rolls drift toward Instinct/Presence, ask whether Agility, Strength, Finesse, or Knowledge better describes the action.

Class Community Ancestry Reveals: Loreborne: spots older legal, heraldic, or ward-craft language under the branding. Underborne: notices service doors, hidden routes, and who built the thing nobody credits. Highborne: reads etiquette, class panic, and reputational risk. Ridgeborne: notices stonework, weight, pressure, and structural weakness. Wildborne: reads the land, animals, and local ecological stress. Elf/Ribbet/Human/Giant/Katari: invite one sensory or social detail from the player's heritage. Sorcerer/Rogue/Warrior/Guardian/Ranger: give each class one table-facing way to shine without changing the plot.
